## Findings
- claim-1: Conditional on the accepted all-degree integral interval/Schur/Pieri presentation for \(p=c=1\), the missing \(k>b:=\min(i,j)\) certificate is established: \((A_+M)_{d+k}=M_{d+k}\) for every \(b<k\le i+j+1\), and \(M_{d+k}=0\) for \(k>i+j+1\).
## Strategy
Assume the all-degree integral interval/Schur/Pieri presentation for \(p=c=1\). Put
\[
d=ij,\quad b=\min(i,j),\quad
\alpha_k=\max(0,k-i),\quad\beta_k=\min(j,k),
\]
\[
P_{x,y}=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{j-x},y)},\qquad
C_x=P_{x,k-x},
\]
and \(T=s_{(i+1)^{j+1}}\).

For \(0\le k\le i+j\),
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=\alpha_k}^{\beta_k}\mathbb ZC_x,
\]
while \(M_{d+i+j+1}=\mathbb ZT\) and \(M_{d+k}=0\) for \(k>i+j+1\).

Since \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\),
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}=\sum_{t=1}^{k}h_tM_{d+k-t}.
\]
For every admissible source \(P_{u,k-t-u}\),
\[
h_tP_{u,k-t-u}
=\mathbf1_{u\in[\alpha_k,\beta_k]}C_u+
 \mathbf1_{u+1\in[\alpha_k,\beta_k]}C_{u+1}.
\]
Thus all multiplication rows are explicitly zero-, one-, or two-term rows.

For \(b<k\le i+j\), at least one boundary singleton exists. If \(k>i\), the rows
\[
C_{\alpha_k},\quad C_u+C_{u+1}\quad(\alpha_k\le u<\beta_k)
\]
form a lower unitriangular \((\beta_k-\alpha_k+1)\)-square matrix, hence determinant \(1\). If \(k\le i\), necessarily \(k>j\), and
\[
C_u+C_{u+1}\quad(\alpha_k\le u<\beta_k),\quad C_{\beta_k}
\]
form an upper unitriangular matrix, again of determinant \(1\). Hence
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}=M_{d+k}\qquad(b<k\le i+j).
\]

At \(k=i+j+1\),
\[
h_tP_{j,i+1-t}=T\qquad(1\le t\le i+1),
\]
so the terminal multiplication matrix is \((1)\), with determinant \(1\), and
\[
(A_+M)_{d+i+j+1}=M_{d+i+j+1}.
\]
For \(k>i+j+1\), \(M_{d+k}=0\), hence both the target degree and its multiplication lattice vanish.

Therefore the requested remaining-degree certificate is established conditional on the stipulated all-degree interval/Schur/Pieri presentation.

## Gaps
The all-degree integral interval presentation, its Schur-basis assertion, and Pieri compatibility are assumed rather than independently source-grounded here.
